etymology: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of 5134 and 5147 through the idea of corrosion or wear, or perhaps rather of a base of 5167 and 5149 through the idea of a crunching sound
definition:
1) to gnaw, crunch, chew raw vegetables or fruits (as nuts, almonds)
    1a) of animals feeding
    1b) of men
 2) to eat
